small_guidance:
- The matmul is the dominant cost (M=1024, N=8192, K=8192). Add larger autotune configs targeting this exact shape: BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 num_stages=4, and BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=128 num_warps=8 num_stages=3. Also try BLOCK_K=128 variants since K=8192 is large and benefits from deeper K-loop pipelining.
- Pre-transpose the weight once (store as K×N layout in __init__) so the inner load on B is along the contiguous K axis without `tl.trans`, and remove the `offs_k < k_remain` mask in the K loop (K=8192 is divisible by all BLOCK_K choices) to cut per-iteration mask overhead.
- Skip the partial+reduce two-kernel design when N fits in a single tile group: with BLOCK_N≥256 there are only 32 tiles; switch to a split-K-free single-kernel that uses atomicMax on a per-row scalar (or persistent loop over N tiles inside the kernel) so the second reduction kernel and the partial buffer disappear.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a persistent / row-stationary kernel: one program per BLOCK_M rows that loops over all N tiles internally, accumulating the running max in registers across pooled tiles. This eliminates the partial buffer, the second reduction kernel launch, and lets the GELU+scale+pool+max fuse into the matmul epilogue with zero extra global traffic.
- Since weight is constant, store weight pre-transposed (K×N contiguous) at module init so the K-loop B-load is a simple contiguous block load (no `tl.trans` of an [N,K] tile), enabling cleaner `tl.dot` with BLOCK_K up to 128 and better stage pipelining.
- Consider FP16/BF16 weight+activation casting inside the kernel epilogue back to FP32 for accumulation — on a 4090 (Ada) tensor cores deliver ~2-4x throughput on fp16 matmul, and the loose 5e-2 tolerance accommodates the precision drop. The matmul is ~137 GFLOPs per batch at this shape, currently ~80 TFLOPs effective; fp16 tensor cores can push >300 TFLOPs.
